The full test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test — the only test class in the project). 

## Summary

I implemented the welcome-notification enqueue on successful owner creation in `OwnerRestControllerV1`:

1. Added a dedicated logger named `NOTIFY`:
   ```java
   private static final Logger notifyLogger = LoggerFactory.getLogger("NOTIFY");
   ```

2. In `addOwner`, after the owner is persisted (so its `memberId` is populated by `saveOwner`) and after the existing audit events, emit the welcome line carrying the owner id and memberId:
   ```java
   notifyLogger.info("welcome: owner id={} memberId={}", owner.getId(), owner.getMemberId());
   ```

This runs only on the successful create path (after the quota/duplicate rejections return early), matching the spec. The `AcceptanceTest.coreEnqueuesWelcome` test — which captures the `NOTIFY` logger and asserts a line contains both the owner id and the memberId read back from `GET /api/owners/{id}` — passes, as does the full suite.

## Summary

I implemented the welcome-notification enqueue on successful owner creation in `OwnerRestControllerV1`:

1. Added a dedicated logger named `NOTIFY`:
   ```java
   private static final Logger notifyLogger = LoggerFactory.getLogger("NOTIFY");
   ```

2. In `addOwner`, after the owner is persisted (so its `memberId` is populated by `saveOwner`) and after the existing audit events, emit the welcome line carrying the owner id and memberId:
   ```java
   notifyLogger.info("welcome: owner id={} memberId={}", owner.getId(), owner.getMemberId());
   ```

This runs only on the successful create path (after the quota/duplicate rejections return early), matching the spec. The `AcceptanceTest.coreEnqueuesWelcome` test — which captures the `NOTIFY` logger and asserts a line contains both the owner id and the memberId read back from `GET /api/owners/{id}` — passes, as does the full suite.
